concern_results.conclusion: Classifier change traced end to end: extraction reads only top-level events with type error or *.failed, pulling message then error.message, deduped and whitespace-collapsed, and the quota/auth greps now cover that file plus stderr with 'usage limit' added; the A1-A6 fixture matrix maps to the observed code paths (item.completed text cannot match, stderr-only quota still matches, no-match still yields unknown_client_failure), every die_inconclusive in the failure block passes run_rc, diagnostic and run_dir in the positions emit_inconclusive maps to argv[5..7], and the static fallback guarantees a non-empty diagnostic when no error event exists.

The verdict-deciding input and the receipt field both exclude nested item events, so packet-quoting model output cannot reach either; raw stderr has no code path into the receipt; redaction (run-root, HOME, URL userinfo, query strings, sk-/Bearer/JWT shapes, shape-based key=value and quoted JSON pairs) is applied where the string is built and verified against a runtime-assembled fixture, so no credential-shaped literal lands in the tree; the preserved directory is mktemp 0700 under TMPDIR and holds only what the in-flight run already held.

Extractor tolerates unreadable files and malformed lines (OSError/ValueError swallowed, partial last line after a timeout kill skipped), builder exits empty on empty input and the shell fallback still emits a bounded non-empty key, so no failure branch can abort the wrapper or omit the diagnostic; timeout, signal, host-path, quota, auth and terminal branches all carry both new fields; success path keeps prior behavior and still deletes the run directory.

New assertions cover each acceptance row including negative-marker checks with redaction fixtures placed on the event stream (so they are not vacuous), bound and single-line checks, truncation, silent-failure fallback, stderr exclusion, directory preservation and mode, and success-receipt absence; RED baseline and four single-predicate mutations are documented with each mutation reding exactly its predicted rows, which is what gives the two baseline-green rows their meaning; one gap: the preservation assertions consume transport_run_dir as a directly usable path, which the finding below covers.

No flag, exit code or reason-code semantics change; emit_inconclusive's two extra positionals are always passed (quoted ${5:-}/${6:-}), so argv indices exist for every legacy call site and payloads are byte-identical when the new args are empty; grep patterns are extended not reordered; new shell constructs (block-level heredocs, case patterns, ${var#...}) parse under Bash 3.2 per the -n evidence, and the heredoc-in-command-substitution trap is documented and avoided.

Change is additive and confined to one wrapper plus its suite and appended register rows; revert restores prior behavior with no migration, persisted state or consumer contract to unwind; the two new receipt keys are relayed by review_gate.py without interpretation (corroborated by the live end-to-end receipt) and egress_schema.py governs only the opencode lane, so no schema edit is required.

The change fixes its own defect class: failed runs now preserve both captured streams in a named run directory and every transport-failure receipt carries the transport's own bounded single-line message plus a fallback that says when nothing was captured, closing the evidence hole that left six receipts across rounds 122-123 unable to falsify the wrong packet-size hypothesis.

The shared-gate steering boundary is contained, not asserted: the classifier input is restricted to transport-authored top-level events, and the mutation removing that restriction turns the packet-derived-text rows red; the egress crossing into committed receipts is bounded at 600 chars, redacted, and cut off from arbitrary stderr entirely, with the redaction-removal mutation reding exactly the redaction rows; CANDIDATE_LOCAL_CODES and all existing reason codes are untouched, so the cascade set changes only for genuinely recognized quota/auth failures.
